fig:I:orbifold.title: The fixed $(3,4,\infty )$ base data. The arrows denote the restriction of $f$ to each indicated fibre, with its scheme multiplicity retained. The ordinary period quotient, finite affine quotients and the paired hexagon are the three actual local models in the common conventions; their overlap maps are fixed there

fig:I:parameter-disc.title: The exact parameter disc for the standard fixed data. The coordinate map is $w=e^{-\pi i c}$ and the coarser coordinate map is $u=w^2$. The imaginary diameter is the fixed locus of $w\mapsto -\bar w$, which is the reflected-family map. The two boundary obstructions use the meridian comparison at the puncture and the intrinsic Albanese nome at the outer circle. The special fibres are over $t=0,1,\infty $ in every member, as indicated in Figure~\ref {fig:I:orbifold}

fig:I:monodromy-domain.title: A fundamental set for the index-twelve monodromy kernel in the real parabolic stabilizer of $d$. The base is a modular fundamental set with its rotation coordinate; the fibre is the indicated Heisenberg parallelepiped. The displayed face maps include the central shears. The representative map and the boundary identifications are proved in \ref {I:monodromy-fundamental-set}; the index twelve occurs in the central fibre coordinate
